newsitem.title: USA: US House will consider ATM fee legislation--Leach.
newsitem.headline: US House will consider ATM fee legislation--Leach.

text.p: House Banking Committee chairman Jim Leach said Monday he would consider legislation to limit fees charged by banks when non-customers use their automated teller machines (ATM).
Senate Banking Committee chairman Alfonse D'Amato introduced a bill last week that would prohibit banks from adding a second charge on non-customer ATM transactions.
"That is the kind of bill we will look at seriously on the House side," the Iowa Republican said in an interview with Reuters Financial Television.
Some House Banking Committee members have previously favored legislation to require clear disclosure of ATM surcharges without proscribing or limiting the practice.

"On the one hand, there's a feeling that competition will solve all of this," Leach said. "But in a market economy such as our own, sometimes there's no competition so you have to be sensitive to consumer protections."
Asked about the bill introduced in the Senate to ban sur charges, Leach said he was "sympathetic to doing something" but added "I have not looked with precision at the D'Amato bill."
